rubric.why: Distinguishes pepsin as the active enzyme.
rubric.description: Pepsin is the active form of the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pepsin as active.

rubric.why: Distinguishes pepsinogen as the inactive form that becomes pepsin.
rubric.description: Pepsinogen is an inactive precursor that is activated by hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pepsinogen as inactive or as the precursor of pepsin.

modelAnswer: Pepsin is the active protein-digesting enzyme in the stomach.
Pepsinogen is its inactive precursor; hydrochloric acid activates it to form pepsin.

rubric.why: Credits two valid protein sources.
rubric.description: Any two suitable sources of protein, such as meat, fish, eggs, milk, pulses, beans or nuts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each pair of valid sources; do not award twice for the same source.

rubric.why: Credits two additional valid protein sources.
rubric.description: Two further suitable sources of protein.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two additional sources not already credited.

modelAnswer: Four sources of protein are meat, fish, eggs and pulses.

items.followUp: State two adaptations of root hairs that help water absorption.

rubric.why: Identifies the main absorptive role of root hairs.
rubric.description: Root hairs absorb water from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that root hairs take up water.

rubric.why: Credits mineral uptake or the adaptation that makes absorption efficient.
rubric.description: They absorb mineral salts and their many fine projections increase the surface area for absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mineral-salt absorption or increased absorptive surface area.

modelAnswer: Root hairs absorb water and dissolved mineral salts from the soil.
Their numerous fine projections provide a large surface area for absorption.

items.followUp: Explain how cohesion helps water move up the xylem.

rubric.why: Identifies the suction or tension generated by water loss from leaves.
rubric.description: Water evaporating from leaves during transpiration creates suction or tension that pulls water upward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration to an upward pull or tension in the xylem.

rubric.why: Identifies the forces that help transmit the pull through the xylem water column.
rubric.description: Cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls help maintain a continuous column of water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for cohesion, adhesion or a continuous water column.

modelAnswer: Evaporation of water from leaves during transpiration creates suction or tension in the xylem.
Cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls maintain a continuous water column, which is pulled upward.

items.followUp: Define any five branches of Biology other than the ones listed in your answer.

rubric.why: Credits a correct definition of morphology.
rubric.description: Morphology is the study of the external form and structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming morphology and describing its study of external form or structure.

rubric.why: Credits a correct definition of anatomy.
rubric.description: Anatomy is the study of the internal structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming anatomy and identifying internal structure.

rubric.why: Credits a correct definition of physiology.
rubric.description: Physiology is the study of the functions of organisms and their parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming physiology and identifying functions.

rubric.why: Credits a correct definition of genetics.
rubric.description: Genetics is the study of inheritance and variation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming genetics and identifying inheritance or variation.

rubric.why: Credits a correct definition of ecology.
rubric.description: Ecology is the study of the relationships of organisms with one another and with their environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ecology and describing organism–environment relationships.

modelAnswer: Morphology is the study of the external form and structure of organisms.
Anatomy is the study of the internal structure of organisms.
Physiology is the study of the functions of organisms and their parts.
Genetics is the study of inheritance and variation.
Ecology is the study of the relationships of organisms with one another and with their environment.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell wall.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic double-layer structure of the membrane.
rubric.description: The cell membrane consists mainly of a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it has two phospholipid layers.

rubric.why: Describes the orientation of phospholipids in the bilayer.
rubric.description: Hydrophilic heads face the watery sides, while hydrophobic tails face inward toward one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the orientation of heads or tails.

rubric.why: Includes the proteins that are part of the membrane structure.
rubric.description: Protein molecules are embedded in or associated with the phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying membrane proteins and their position in the membrane.

rubric.why: Credits the accepted model or a key property of the membrane.
rubric.description: The membrane is described by the fluid mosaic model and is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the fluid mosaic model or stating that the membrane is selectively permeable.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
The hydrophilic heads of phospholipids face the watery environments on both sides of the membrane.
The hydrophobic tails face inward toward one another.
This arrangement is described by the fluid mosaic model, and the membrane is selectively permeable.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature and pH affect enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of temperature on enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Enzyme activity increases with temperature up to an optimum; higher temperatures can denature the enzyme and reduce activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an optimum or heat denaturation and its effect on activity.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of pH on enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Each enzyme has an optimum pH; values above or below it alter the active site and lower activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an optimum pH or explaining that unsuitable pH lowers activity.

rubric.why: Explains how substrate availability affects the reaction rate.
rubric.description: Increasing substrate concentration increases the rate until the enzyme's active sites are saturated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increase in rate or the saturation limit.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of enzyme amount on reaction rate.
rubric.description: Increasing enzyme concentration increases the reaction rate when sufficient substrate is available.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking more enzyme or active sites to a higher rate.

rubric.why: Credits the effect of inhibitors on enzyme action.
rubric.description: Inhibitors reduce enzyme activity, for example by blocking an active site or interfering with the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that inhibitors lower enzyme activity or explaining how they do so.

modelAnswer: Temperature: enzyme activity rises as temperature increases up to the enzyme's optimum; above this, the enzyme may denature and its activity falls.
pH: each enzyme works best at an optimum pH; a pH that is too high or too low changes the active site and reduces activity.
Substrate concentration: increasing substrate concentration raises the reaction rate until the enzyme's active sites are saturated.
Enzyme concentration: increasing the amount of enzyme raises the reaction rate if enough substrate is available.
Inhibitors: inhibitors reduce enzyme activity by interfering with the enzyme or blocking its active site.

rubric.why: Identifies the subject matter of microbiology.
rubric.description: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining microbiology as the study of microorganisms or microbes.

rubric.why: Identifies the subject matter of morphology.
rubric.description: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms, especially their external form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining morphology in terms of the form or structure of organisms.

modelAnswer: Microbiology is the branch of Biology that studies microorganisms.
Morphology is the branch of Biology that studies the form and structure of organisms.
